chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudaylah ibn Ayyub, from 'Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Maysarah, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If a man encounters a woman in a remote place (al-fala) who has no guardian (wali) for her, and he asks her,

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْفَلاَة: A remote or open place, often implying a lack of local guardians.
key_terms.الْمُصَدَّقَةُ عَلَى نَفْسِهَا: The woman who validates/confirms her own marriage contract.

ai.seo_question: How is a woman's marriage contracted if she has no guardian (wali)?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the mechanism of *al-musaddiqah 'ala nafsaha* (self-validation), where a woman without a male guardian (*wali*) can contract her own marriage by declaring her status to a suitor. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes her as her own guardian in the absence of an appointed one, ensuring the validity of the contract through her explicit consent and declaration. This ruling highlights the flexibility in marital contracts for women lacking a natural guardian, emphasizing their agency in legal proceedings.
